route._jar_unpinned: 11 September 2026: this pinned ~/bin/freerouting-1.9.0.jar, the STOCK jar, which set FR_JAR and so bypassed route_one's own choice AND its refusal. Our 1.9.0 build writes a session after every pass; the stock one writes one only when the whole job ends, so a run that is cut leaves nothing, which is what every NO_SESSION round in the record is. Unpinned: route_one takes the patched jar when the host has it and refuses when it does not, unless FR_REQUIRE_MESH=0 says otherwise deliberately.
route._ripup_why: 14 September 2026: C12 ended 0 hard with two opens, /PWM1 and /HB2, and both pads sit in open ground (nothing within 2.12 mm of TP29, nothing but its partner's tracks within 1.65 mm of R44). A board-wide stub search at a 0.1 mm grid on all three routing layers, at the panel's own class clearance of 0.127 rather than the tool's old 0.16 literal, finds no path for either: the lanes are not there and no closure will make them. The router is deterministic, so more passes repeat the result and only a different rules file is a different solution. via_costs 100 was round two's remedy and took 12 opens to 4; the rip-up cost is the second lever fr_rules writes and has never been moved on this board. 10 against the default 100 makes the router far more willing to tear up and re-lay, which is what a board whose strips are full needs.
route._ripup_measured: 14 September 2026: the rip-up cost at 10 against the default 100, same copper, same 45 passes: 0 hard and 59 unrouted of 133 nets with 133 vias, against C12's 4 unrouted with 385. A router that tears up freely never converges on this board, so the lever is real and it points the other way. It is not tried higher either: the evidence says this board is at a congestion cliff where MORE search wanders, which is the second reading of the same thing. C11's 30 passes left 3 unrouted and its finish closed two; C12's 45 left 4 and the finish closed two; C13's 45 at ripup 10 left 59.
